gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-questrial: Questrial keeps its letters open and stencil-flat, tall in the body with short stalks above. Questrial next to Edo SZ feels like a quiet modern voice standing beside a heading with cast-iron stature.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-radio-canada: Radio Canada draws its tall, full c, s and z with a steady line and clear curve endings. And Edo SZ, the display heading above it, holds one constant stroke width in a classic, cultural voice.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-radio-canada-big: Tall, plain and sturdy. Radio Canada Big fills each line with a monoline skeleton and terminals clear of the stem, so Radio Canada Big stays easy to follow across long paragraphs under Edo SZ.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-readex-pro: Readex Pro spreads broad gaps at its terminals and holds a calm, unvarying weight from one word to the next. Edo SZ sits above it with cast-iron lowercase stature.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-roboto: Contemporary lines run through Roboto, with generous mouths on its round letters. Roboto sits under Edo SZ, whose cultural, classic strokes keep their width through every turn.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-ruda: Ruda brings a sizable x-height and a wire-like monoline skeleton, with wide-mouthed rounds in the lowercase. Edo SZ makes a statement with cast-iron stature, while Ruda simply reads comfortably.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-saira: Neutral and clean, Saira lets you see through each s while its rounded letters climb toward the top line. Saira sits beneath Edo SZ, a heading with a wire-like monoline skeleton and classic stature.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-sarpanch: Approachable Sarpanch opens the mouth of its lowercase e clearly. Edo SZ above it has no calligraphic thinning at all, so its cultural, classic lettering and that compact body text sit together comfortably.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Bold-looking and light-looking strokes never mix inside a word in Edo SZ, giving it cast-iron stature. Schibsted Grotesk then handles the reading, with big open e and a shapes and terminals that never close in.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-sen: Modern and tall, Sen traces each lowercase letter with a constant line. Edo SZ is best at classic, cultural statement lettering, while Sen is a plain sans that keeps curved strokes ending before they turn inward.
